1 big thing: SpaceX aims for historic rocket catch
 
SpaceX's mega rocket Starship ahead of today's test flight from Starbase, Texas. Photo: Eric Gay/AP

SpaceX is about to try to catch both its next-gen Starship rocket and its Super Heavy booster back at their launch pad for the first time, Alex Fitzpatrick reports.

A successful attempt would make rocketry history — and mark a huge step toward realizing SpaceX's vision of Starship as a fully reusable, 171-foot space launch behemoth.

  • That reusability could dramatically cut launch costs, potentially ushering in a new era of commercial spaceflight.

⏱️ Starship is scheduled to launch from South Texas as early as 5:45 p.m. ET this afternoon, barring weather or mechanical troubles.

  • The Super Heavy booster will separate and return for a catch attempt a few minutes after launch. (SpaceX has caught Super Heavy before, but never Starship.)

🛰️ Starship will then orbit Earth about 14 times over 22 hours, while deploying new satellites for SpaceX's Starlink internet service.

  • It will then head Earthward, flip itself upright and attempt to land in the huge mechanical "chopstick" arms of its launch tower.

✅ Reality check: A test flight this novel leaves lots of room for things to go wrong.

2. 👩‍💻 Outlook crawls back to life
 
Illustration: Aïda Amer/Axios. Stock: Getty Images

Microsoft says it's making progress in bringing its popular workplace software back online as a global outage reaches its second day.

  • The outage, which has affected Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot, has left millions of people, institutions and businesses worldwide without access to their email and other tools.

📧 Microsoft said today: "We're seeing encouraging recovery progress, with service availability and email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected Microsoft 365 infrastructure."

  • The company added that users may have "intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery as mitigation progresses across the remaining affected infrastructure."

👾 The company hasn't fully explained the outage, but says there's no indication it was caused by malicious activity.

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
Pope Leo XIV greets onlookers before celebrating Mass today in Pampas de Pimentel, Peru. Photo: Ernesto Benavides/AFP via Getty Images
  1. ⛪️ Pope Leo XIV returned to his beloved former diocese of Chiclayo, Peru, today in an emotional homecoming that underscored his love for his flock there. Go deeper.
  2. 📺 Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC's "Squawk Box" today that while his department and others agreed on placing Megaspeed on a special list of companies that pose national security concerns, the Commerce Department "has the pen." Bessent didn't deny reports of tension with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who has come under scrutiny for his inaction over Megaspeed. Get the latest ... Watch the clip.
  3. 🇮🇱 The director of Israeli spy agency Mossad is in Washington today for talks with senior Trump administration officials about the war in Iran, according to three sources with knowledge of the matter. More from Barak Ravid.
 
 
4. 🎬 1 film thing: Glenn Close gets honorary Oscar
 
Glenn Close in March 1989. Photo: John Downing/Hulton Archive via Getty Images

Iconic actress Glenn Close, 79, will receive an honorary Oscar at Sunday's Governors Awards, after eight lifetime nominations but no wins.

  • Close tells AP: "My first reaction was I don't need a consolation prize. And my second reaction was, I don't know ... do I want to end my loss record?"

🍿 Honorary Oscars, also known as Academy Honorary Awards, aren't given for a specific film, but for a body of work and contributions to the motion picture industry.
